info.text: Interactive check questions for Lesson 13.3: Multi-Modal Publishing, Minimal Computing, and Long-Term Archiving.

name.text: 01 Question: The Multi-Modal Vision: Publishing Beyond a Single Screen

questiontext.text: Why must a true digital scholarly edition output to multiple distinct publication formats?

generalfeedback.text: A digital scholarly edition must compile into interactive web, offline standalone, and print-ready formats from a single master TEI XML file.

answer.text: Different readers require different environments, such as interactive websites for study, offline packages for travel, and print PDFs for formal citation.

feedback.text: Correct. Compiling multiple formats from a single master XML file ensures broad access while preserving data consistency.

answer.text: Federal law prohibits publishing scholarship on more than one computer monitor.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multi-modal publishing is a scholarly best practice, not a legal restriction.

answer.text: Digital editions must delete their underlying XML after creating a website.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The master TEI XML file is preserved permanently as the single source of truth.

answer.text: Readers are only allowed to read historical documents on smartphones.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multi-modal editions support mobile devices, desktop monitors, and physical printed books.

name.text: 02 Question: Medium-Specific Affordances: Screen vs. Page vs. Raw Data

questiontext.text: What is the scholarly affordance of a fixed printed page compared to an interactive digital screen?

generalfeedback.text: Understanding medium-specific affordances allows editors to optimize commentary, layouts, and citations for screens, printed pages, and data streams.

answer.text: A printed page provides fixed, permanent layout with stable page and line numbers that never suffer from link rot or battery failure.

feedback.text: Correct. While screens excel at interactivity and zooming, print provides permanent, distraction-free reading grids.

answer.text: A printed page can play high-definition video animations of scribes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Physical paper cannot display video; that is an affordance of digital screens.

answer.text: A printed page automatically rewrites its sentences every five years.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Print pages are static and permanent once printed.

answer.text: A printed page can only be read inside a bank vault.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Print books are portable and universally readable without electricity.

name.text: 03 Question: What is Minimal Computing in Digital Humanities?

questiontext.text: How does minimal computing prevent digital editions from disappearing when grant funding ends?

generalfeedback.text: Minimal computing ensures digital editions survive for decades by using simple static files that require zero server maintenance or hosting budgets.

answer.text: It uses static files and open formats that require zero ongoing server maintenance, database costs, or administrative upkeep.

feedback.text: Correct. Plain HTML, CSS, and TEI XML files survive for decades on free static storage without server crashes.

answer.text: It forces researchers to type all documents on mechanical typewriters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Minimal computing uses modern digital tools like Git, HTML5, and TEI XML.

answer.text: It deletes all images and commentary to make files smaller than one kilobyte.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Minimal computing supports high-resolution images and rich scholarship without server bloat.

answer.text: It requires paying expensive monthly fees to cloud software corporations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Minimal computing explicitly avoids expensive recurring subscription fees.

name.text: 04 Question: The Fragility of the Digital Archive

questiontext.text: What is 'link rot', and why is it a severe hazard for digital scholarship?

generalfeedback.text: Digital editions protect against link rot and format obsolescence by using open plain-text TEI XML and permanent digital identifiers.

answer.text: The process by which web addresses change or expire over time, causing scholarly links to return broken 404 errors.

feedback.text: Correct. Over half of academic web links break within ten years; persistent DOIs prevent this decay.

answer.text: The physical rusting of computer cables in humid library basements.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Link rot refers to broken web hyperlinks and expired domain names.

answer.text: A computer virus that deletes punctuation marks from historical texts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Link rot is caused by changing web URLs and server migrations.

answer.text: The inability of modern printers to print digital documents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Link rot affects web links, not printer hardware.

name.text: 05 Question: Compiling Standalone Offline HTML Packages

questiontext.text: What are the contents and benefits of a standalone offline HTML package?

generalfeedback.text: Standalone offline packages bundle HTML, CSS, scripts, and images into portable zip files that run anywhere without internet access.

answer.text: It bundles HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and optimized images into a portable zip file that runs anywhere without an internet connection.

feedback.text: Correct. Scholars can open index.html directly from a laptop or USB drive during archival fieldwork.

answer.text: It contains an encrypted password that only university presidents can open.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Offline packages are designed for open, frictionless access.

answer.text: It requires an active internet connection to download every paragraph.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Offline packages are completely self-contained and run without network access.

answer.text: It converts all historical documents into spreadsheet financial ledgers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The package preserves the full reading layout, facsimiles, and commentary.

name.text: 06 Question: Offline Client-Side Search with Lunr.js

questiontext.text: How does client-side search with Lunr.js operate without a live database server?

generalfeedback.text: Client-side search tools like Lunr.js enable instant full-text search inside the browser without requiring a database server or internet connection.

answer.text: It searches a pre-built static JSON index entirely inside the user's web browser memory in milliseconds.

feedback.text: Correct. This provides instant full-text search offline with zero server processing or hosting costs.

answer.text: It sends every search query to a remote supercomputer via satellite.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Lunr.js runs 100% locally inside the web browser.

answer.text: It requires readers to manually read through the entire dictionary before searching.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The pre-compiled JSON index allows instant computational lookups.

answer.text: It only searches for numbers and ignores all historical words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Lunr.js provides comprehensive full-text search across all transcribed words and notes.

name.text: 07 Question: Print-Ready PDF Publishing with CSS Paged Media and Typst

questiontext.text: What advantages do modern typesetting tools like Typst and CSS Paged Media offer over legacy LaTeX?

generalfeedback.text: Modern tools like Typst and CSS Paged Media convert TEI XML into elegant, print-ready PDF volumes with automatic page numbering and running headers.

answer.text: They provide clean, readable syntax, rapid compilation, and automatic page layouts with running headers and footnotes.

feedback.text: Correct. Modern tools simplify the creation of professional print codex volumes without LaTeX's dense syntax.

answer.text: They prevent users from printing documents on physical paper.

feedback.text: Incorrect. These tools are specifically designed to generate high-quality print-ready PDFs.

answer.text: They only work if the document contains zero words.

feedback.text: Incorrect. They typeset complex books, critical editions, and scholarly articles.

answer.text: They require users to manually calculate the coordinates of every letter on the page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Typst and CSS Paged Media calculate page breaks and line layouts automatically.

name.text: 08 Question: Structuring the Print Critical Apparatus

questiontext.text: How is a traditional critical footnote formatted at the bottom of a printed edition page?

generalfeedback.text: Print editions structure commentary as a critical apparatus at the bottom of the page, citing the lemma with a closing square bracket and clear historical notes.

answer.text: It cites the lemma from the text followed by a closing square bracket, then provides the philological or historical explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. For example: '1 truckhouse] A British colonial trading post established in 1752...'.

answer.text: It hides the note text in invisible white ink.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Print footnotes must be clearly visible and legible at the bottom of the page.

answer.text: It replaces historical notes with modern advertisements.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scholarly editions present verified historical and philological commentary.

answer.text: It prints all notes upside down at the top of the title page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Standard apparatus notes appear as numbered footnotes directly below the referenced text.

name.text: 09 Question: PDF/A: The Archival Standard for Digital Documents

questiontext.text: Why is PDF/A required for permanent digital preservation rather than standard PDF?

generalfeedback.text: Compiling to the PDF/A archival standard embeds all fonts and metadata directly inside the file, guaranteeing permanent visual preservation.

answer.text: PDF/A mandates 100% embedded fonts and prohibits external scripts, guaranteeing that pages render identically decades into the future.

feedback.text: Correct. Standard PDFs can break when system fonts or external links disappear; PDF/A is self-contained.

answer.text: PDF/A automatically translates documents into ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. PDF/A preserves the exact visual appearance of the original text.

answer.text: PDF/A files can only be opened once before they erase themselves.

feedback.text: Incorrect. PDF/A is an ISO standard designed for permanent, indefinite preservation.

answer.text: PDF/A requires paying annual royalty fees to printer manufacturers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. PDF/A is an open international standard freely supported by modern readers.

name.text: 10 Question: The FAIR Data Principles: Findable and Accessible

questiontext.text: What actions satisfy the Findable and Accessible principles in our capstone digital edition?

generalfeedback.text: The Findable and Accessible principles ensure your digital edition can be discovered through persistent DOIs and downloaded freely by scholars worldwide.

answer.text: Depositing the edition on Zenodo with rich metadata and a persistent DOI, and making files freely downloadable via GitHub.

feedback.text: Correct. This ensures search engines can locate the project and scholars can retrieve it without paywalls.

answer.text: Keeping the edition hidden on a password-protected personal thumb drive.

feedback.text: Incorrect. FAIR principles require research data to be discoverable and openly accessible.

answer.text: Selling access to the XML transcription for one hundred dollars per download.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Open accessibility avoids commercial paywalls and restrictions.

answer.text: Deleting the project repository as soon as the final grade is submitted.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Archiving ensures permanent preservation and scholarly citation.

name.text: 11 Question: The FAIR Data Principles: Interoperable and Reusable

questiontext.text: How does using standard TEI XML and explicit open licensing fulfill Interoperability and Reusability?

generalfeedback.text: Encoding in TEI XML and declaring explicit open licenses satisfies the Interoperable and Reusable principles, empowering global scholars to build upon your work.

answer.text: Standard TEI XML allows external software to process the data, while open licenses (CC BY, CC0) legally define how others may reuse it.

feedback.text: Correct. Interoperability enables computational data sharing; reusability provides legal clarity and documentation.

answer.text: It forces all other researchers to use the exact same operating system as the editor.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Open formats ensure data can be processed across any operating system.

answer.text: It prohibits anyone from ever reading the document again.

feedback.text: Incorrect. FAIR data principles maximize global scholarly reuse.

answer.text: It converts all XML tags into proprietary closed binary data.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Interoperability requires standard, open semantic formats.

name.text: 12 Question: Persistent Identifiers: Why URLs Break and DOIs Endure

questiontext.text: Why does a persistent DOI remain stable even if a university changes its web servers?

generalfeedback.text: Persistent DOIs protect your edition against link rot by providing permanent redirection through the international DOI registry.

answer.text: The DOI points to an international registry that automatically redirects users to the current live address of the files.

feedback.text: Correct. If files move to a new server, updating the redirect target in the registry preserves all published citations.

answer.text: The DOI physically stops computer servers from ever being turned off.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Servers can change; the DOI registry handles redirection seamlessly.

answer.text: A DOI only works if printed on special archival parchment.

feedback.text: Incorrect. DOIs function digitally across web browsers, catalogues, and printed citations.

answer.text: A DOI deletes all previous versions of a website to save disk space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. DOIs provide permanent, versioned citation anchors.

name.text: 13 Question: Depositing Research Data with Zenodo

questiontext.text: What institutional backing and capabilities make Zenodo the premier repository for open editions?

generalfeedback.text: Zenodo provides free, permanent archival storage and mints an official citable DOI for your capstone digital edition.

answer.text: Operated permanently by CERN, Zenodo provides free archival storage, DataCite DOIs, and indexing across global library catalogues.

feedback.text: Correct. CERN's long-term commitment ensures your capstone edition remains safe and citable indefinitely.

answer.text: Zenodo is a commercial social network that sells student research to advertisers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Zenodo is an open-access, non-profit academic repository operated by CERN.

answer.text: Zenodo charges students five hundred dollars for every uploaded XML file.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Zenodo is completely free for open-access research datasets up to 50 GB.

answer.text: Zenodo only accepts projects written in computer machine code.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Zenodo welcomes humanities editions, datasets, code, and PDF codices.

name.text: 14 Question: Linking GitHub to Zenodo for Automated Releases

questiontext.text: How does connecting GitHub to Zenodo streamline the digital publication workflow?

generalfeedback.text: The GitHub-Zenodo integration automatically archives tagged releases, minting permanent DOIs without manual file uploads.

answer.text: Creating a tagged release in GitHub triggers Zenodo to automatically archive a snapshot and mint a permanent DOI.

feedback.text: Correct. This automates the archival pipeline, providing both Concept DOIs and version-specific DOIs.

answer.text: It automatically writes your entire final paper without any human input.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The integration manages release archiving, not textual authoring.

answer.text: It deletes your local files as soon as a release is tagged.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Your repository remains intact; Zenodo simply archives a frozen copy.

answer.text: It requires re-typing the entire XML document into a web form.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The transfer is automated through GitHub's API.

name.text: 15 Question: Structuring the Capstone Edition Portfolio

questiontext.text: What five core components must be included in your final Capstone Edition Portfolio?

generalfeedback.text: The final capstone portfolio unifies your master TEI XML, archival facsimiles, responsive web edition, print PDF, and documentation into a single citable release.

answer.text: Master TEI XML, high-resolution facsimiles, responsive web app, print PDF codex, and complete README/LEDGER documentation.

feedback.text: Correct. This comprehensive bundle satisfies both digital humanities standards and traditional philological rigor.

answer.text: A handwritten diary, five blank floppy disks, and a receipt from a local coffee shop.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The portfolio consists of formal digital textual files and documentation.

answer.text: Only an unformatted Word document with no XML markup or images.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The capstone evaluates your mastery of TEI XML, web layouts, and archiving.

answer.text: A video recording of the student typing at their desk with no project files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The submission is an integrated repository containing data, media, and code.

name.text: 16 Question: The Project Ledger (LEDGER.md): Documenting Decisions

questiontext.text: Why is maintaining a project ledger (LEDGER.md) essential for scholarly reproducibility?

generalfeedback.text: The project ledger records your editorial decisions and methodological reasoning, ensuring scholarly transparency and reproducibility.

answer.text: It documents settled decisions, regularization rules, and computational logs, establishing a transparent chain of custody for your scholarship.

feedback.text: Correct. Without a ledger, the rationale behind editorial choices is lost over time, preventing rigorous peer review.

answer.text: It lists the daily lunch schedule of everyone in the university building.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The ledger records scholarly and technical editorial decisions.

answer.text: It encrypts editorial mistakes so peer reviewers cannot discover them.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The ledger ensures transparent, honest documentation of research methods.

answer.text: It replaces the primary historical text with personal opinions.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The ledger is a paratext documenting editorial governance.

name.text: 17 Question: Open Access Licensing in Practice: CC BY, CC0, and MIT

questiontext.text: Why is multi-tiered licensing recommended across the different asset layers of a digital edition?

generalfeedback.text: Multi-tiered open access licensing protects your scholarly authorship while permitting global research reuse and library indexing.

answer.text: It applies CC BY to prose for attribution, CC0 to metadata for library indexing, and MIT to scripts for software reuse.

feedback.text: Correct. Different asset types have different legal requirements; multi-tiered licensing handles each appropriately.

answer.text: It prevents anyone outside Canada from viewing the project website.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Open licenses enable global research access and collaboration.

answer.text: It requires readers to sign a physical contract before reading each page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Creative Commons licenses operate automatically without paperwork.

answer.text: It surrenders all student rights to commercial database corporations.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multi-tiered licensing preserves student attribution while encouraging ethical open reuse.

name.text: 18 Question: Cohort Archiving: Ace's French Revolutionary Decree

questiontext.text: What key metadata coordinates should Ace include when depositing the 1791 assignat decree on Zenodo?

generalfeedback.text: Ace's Zenodo deposit preserves the 1791 French Revolutionary currency decree with complete archival coordinates, bilingual XML, and a citable DOI.

answer.text: Title, National Assembly context, Imprimerie Royale printing, Archives nationales de France custody, and monetary policy keywords.

feedback.text: Correct. Precise archival coordinates and historical keywords ensure the deposit is discoverable by French Revolutionary historians.

answer.text: Listing the document as an anonymous twentieth-century Canadian novel.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Metadata must accurately reflect the 1791 French Revolutionary legislative artifact.

answer.text: Claiming the document was written by King Louis XIV in 1650.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The decree was passed by the National Assembly in June 1791.

answer.text: Omitting all dates and keywords so nobody can search for the document.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Rich metadata is required to satisfy FAIR data principles.

name.text: 19 Question: Cohort Archiving: Olyvia's Maud Lewis Letter

questiontext.text: What archival coordinates and cultural context define Olyvia's Maud Lewis Zenodo deposit?

generalfeedback.text: Olyvia's Zenodo deposit preserves Maud Lewis's 1967 handwritten letter, providing art historians with high-resolution facsimiles, diplomatic text, and a permanent DOI.

answer.text: Marshalltown cottage life, roadside painting sales, Leonard Kinnear correspondence, and links to Art Gallery of Nova Scotia holdings.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the material and epistolary significance of Maud Lewis's folk art correspondence.

answer.text: Describing the letter as an official British military battle order from the War of 1812.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The artifact is a 1967 personal letter by Nova Scotia folk artist Maud Lewis.

answer.text: Deleting Maud Lewis's name and attributing the letter to an anonymous politician.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Olyvia's edition honors Maud Lewis's unique voice and artistic legacy.

answer.text: Stating that the letter was written on stone tablets in ancient Rome.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The letter was written on personal paper stationery in Digby County in 1967.

name.text: 20 Question: Cohort Archiving: Andromeda's 1752 Peace and Friendship Treaty

questiontext.text: How does Andromeda's Zenodo deposit document the archival custody and legal significance of the 1752 treaty?

generalfeedback.text: Andromeda's Zenodo deposit establishes a permanent, open-access digital edition of the 1752 treaty with legal commentary and high-resolution totem facsimiles.

answer.text: By citing Nova Scotia Archives RG 1 vol 430, documenting Cope-Hopson negotiations, and highlighting Mi'kmaw totem marks and treaty rights.

feedback.text: Correct. Complete legal metadata and high-resolution totem facsimiles ensure the deposit serves legal scholars and Indigenous communities.

answer.text: By presenting the treaty as a private real estate bill of sale.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The 1752 treaty is a sovereign nation-to-nation peace and friendship agreement.

answer.text: By claiming the treaty was signed in Paris between France and Spain.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The treaty was negotiated and signed at Halifax, Nova Scotia.

answer.text: By omitting the names of Mi'kmaw leaders who signed the agreement.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The edition specifically highlights Chief Jean-Baptiste Cope and Mi'kmaw signatories.

name.text: 21 Question: Creating a GitHub Release for Your Edition

questiontext.text: What steps are required to publish an official tagged release in your GitHub repository?

generalfeedback.text: Publishing a GitHub Release freezes an official versioned snapshot of your edition and attaches downloadable offline zip and PDF files.

answer.text: Ensure changes are committed, tag a version (v1.0.0), write detailed release notes, and attach offline zip and PDF files.

feedback.text: Correct. Publishing a release creates a permanent historical milestone and triggers automated archiving.

answer.text: Delete the repository and re-upload files as an anonymous email attachment.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Releases are created cleanly within the GitHub web interface or command line.

answer.text: Print out the code on paper and mail it to GitHub headquarters in California.

feedback.text: Incorrect. GitHub Releases are managed digitally through Git version tags.

answer.text: Change all passwords so nobody can ever log into the repository again.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Releases mark public milestones for open research access.

name.text: 22 Question: Preparing Your Web Edition for GitHub Pages

questiontext.text: How do you deploy your compiled static web edition to GitHub Pages?

generalfeedback.text: GitHub Pages provides free, permanent static web hosting directly from your repository, making your edition instantly accessible to the public.

answer.text: Place compiled files in docs/, enable Pages in repository settings pointing to main/docs, and obtain your live URL.

feedback.text: Correct. GitHub Pages builds and serves your static edition over HTTPS in less than a minute.

answer.text: Purchase an expensive dedicated database server from a commercial cloud provider.

feedback.text: Incorrect. GitHub Pages is completely free and requires no database setup.

answer.text: Convert all HTML files into password-protected Microsoft Word files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. GitHub Pages serves open standard HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

answer.text: Send a paper letter to the university registrar requesting server permissions.

feedback.text: Incorrect. GitHub Pages is self-service and activates instantly in repository settings.

name.text: 23 Question: Documenting AI Provenance and Human-in-the-Loop Audit

questiontext.text: Why must your README.md include a formal AI disclosure and human-in-the-loop audit protocol?

generalfeedback.text: Full disclosure of AI models and human-in-the-loop verification protocols establishes scholarly trust and upholds academic integrity.

answer.text: Methodological transparency demands full disclosure of computational tools, proving that human editors verified all AI outputs against primary sources.

feedback.text: Correct. Academic integrity requires transparent disclosure of models, prompts, dates, and verification reference works.

answer.text: Using computational tools is strictly forbidden in universities and results in automatic expulsion.

feedback.text: Incorrect. AI tools are valuable when disclosed transparently and audited by human editors.

answer.text: To allow computer models to claim legal copyright ownership over historical texts.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Human editors retain copyright and academic responsibility for the edition.

answer.text: To prove that human beings did not read any part of the historical document.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The human-in-the-loop protocol proves that human editors audited every fact.

name.text: 24 Question: Archival Checksums: Verifying Data Integrity with SHA-256

questiontext.text: How do SHA-256 cryptographic checksums protect digital editions against bit rot and file tampering?

generalfeedback.text: SHA-256 checksums provide cryptographic proof of data integrity, allowing scholars to verify that downloaded files are authentic and uncorrupted.

answer.text: They provide unique mathematical fingerprints for each file; if even a single byte changes, the checksum changes completely.

feedback.text: Correct. Verifying checksums with sha256sum -c proves that downloaded files are authentic and uncorrupted.

answer.text: They automatically compress all files into tiny images.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Checksums are cryptographic hashes used for verification, not compression.

answer.text: They scramble the text so nobody can read it without paying a fee.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Checksums verify integrity without encrypting or altering file contents.

answer.text: They predict the future weather in the archive building.

feedback.text: Incorrect. SHA-256 is a mathematical hashing algorithm.

name.text: 25 Question: Writing a Professional Citation for Your Digital Edition

questiontext.text: What elements are essential when providing a Chicago-style citation for your digital edition?

generalfeedback.text: Providing formal Chicago, MLA, and APA citations with persistent DOIs enables future researchers to cite your digital scholarship accurately.

answer.text: Editor name, italicized edition title with [Digital Scholarly Edition], institution, year, and persistent Zenodo DOI URL.

feedback.text: Correct. For example: Penner, Andromeda, ed. The 1752 Peace and Friendship Treaty... https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1234567.

answer.text: Only the student's first name and the date they submitted the assignment.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Formal citations include full editor names, titles, institution, year, and DOIs.

answer.text: A link to a personal social media account with no project information.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Citations must point to persistent scholarly repositories like Zenodo.

answer.text: A statement that the text is secret and must not be cited in academic papers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Providing citations encourages other scholars to reference your research.

name.text: 26 Question: Peer Review and Scholarly Evaluation of Digital Editions

questiontext.text: What key criteria do organizations like the IDE use to evaluate digital scholarly editions?

generalfeedback.text: Peer review of digital editions evaluates both philological rigor and computational sustainability, requiring valid XML, clear policies, and durable archiving.

answer.text: Methodological transparency, TEI schema validity, material witness fidelity, and technical sustainability via open formats.

feedback.text: Correct. Digital editions are reviewed both as philological scholarship and as sustainable data architecture.

answer.text: How many animated cartoon characters appear on the homepage.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Academic review focuses on textual fidelity, rigor, and technical design.

answer.text: Whether the website requires an expensive monthly paid subscription.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reviewers value open access, standards compliance, and long-term durability.

answer.text: Whether the edition was written entirely in modern slang.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Scholarly editions maintain absolute fidelity to historical primary sources.

name.text: 27 Question: Final Quality Gate: Pre-Deposit Verification Checklist

questiontext.text: What five verification gates must pass before tagging a production release and depositing files?

generalfeedback.text: The pre-deposit verification checklist guarantees that your master XML, web layouts, print PDF, and metadata are 100% verified before permanent release.

answer.text: Submitting the assignment without opening or testing any of the compiled files.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A quality gate requires active verification before submission.
